$schema-comment: Source of truth for which glib/gobject symbols this project renames and re-exports as vips_g_* wrappers (see extra/glib_wrapper.c/.h in vendor/sharp-libvips), and why each one is there. /rebuild-for-version and any human doing a version bump should diff a fresh grep of sharp's source against this list, not against the prose in README.md.

symbols.name: g_object_ref
symbols.originDetail: cplusplus/include/vips/VImage8.h, VObject smart-pointer class (constructor/copy-assignment) — header-only, inlined into sharp.node wherever vips::VImage is used
symbols.riskDetail: Confirmed root cause of the original segfault. Touches a VipsImage's embedded GObject refcount/type-registration state, which lives in whichever glib copy registered that GType (libvips's private one).
symbols.foundVia: grep (guessed first, then confirmed as the crash cause during initial diagnosis)

symbols.name: g_object_unref
symbols.riskDetail: Same reasoning as g_object_ref — must come from the same glib copy that did the matching ref.
symbols.foundVia: grep (guessed first, then confirmed as the crash cause during initial diagnosis)

symbols.name: g_malloc
symbols.riskDetail: Modern glib (post-2.46) is a thin passthrough to the system malloc/free with no private allocator state, so mixing copies here is likely safe in practice. Wrapped anyway since the mechanism already exists and the marginal cost is one line.

symbols.name: g_free
symbols.originDetail: src/common.cc, FreeCallback (paired with the g_malloc allocations above via napi Buffer::NewOrCopy)
symbols.riskDetail: Must match whichever allocator did the corresponding g_malloc — see that entry.

symbols.name: g_signal_connect_data
symbols.originDetail: src/common.cc, SetTimeout() — sharp's own source calls the g_signal_connect macro, which expands to this function
symbols.riskDetail: Connects a signal on a VipsImage (a libvips-private GObject); signal IDs are looked up in glib's global signal registry, which lives in whichever copy registered the GType. Not independently crash-tested in isolation, but the same class of risk as g_object_ref's confirmed failure mode.

symbols.name: g_log_set_handler
symbols.originDetail: src/sharp.cc, init() — registers VipsWarningCallback for the "VIPS" log domain
symbols.riskDetail: Not a crash risk, but libvips's own internal g_warning()/g_log() calls go through its private glib. Registering the handler via a different glib copy means it silently never fires — no crash, just broken warning capture.

symbols.name: g_utf8_validate
symbols.originDetail: src/metadata.cc, XMP metadata validation before returning it as a string
symbols.riskDetail: Missed on the first grep pass entirely. Only surfaced as a runtime `undefined symbol` dlopen failure when running sharp's own test suite (test/unit/metadata.js) against the rebuilt addon — a clean build and a passing git apply were not sufficient evidence the wrapper set was complete.

headersChecked.note: Other libvips public C++ headers pulled in via <vips/vips8> were checked for the same inline-glib-call pattern VImage8.h has. None had it, as of the target versions above.
